correctness.rationale: Aoki's full primary PDF was inspected and confirms the exact definitions: W(S,C) is the interval family satisfying both extremal boundary conditions; a pair is saturated exactly when W(S,C) is a singleton; bar-omega is |Max(C\S)|+|Min(S\C)|; and Theorem 6.5 gives gldim Lambda_P as the maximum bar-omega over saturated pairs. For a star, every interval is a singleton leaf or a center-containing subset. The submitted case split gives bar-omega<=r for r>=2. Taking S=lower leaves plus center and C=center plus upper leaves has S union C=P; Aoki's Proposition 6.1 says W has minimum S union C when nonempty, so the exhibited P forces W={P}, and bar-omega=r. The r=1 case gives 2. The maximum-degree corollary uses the full subposet on a vertex and its Hasse neighbors, which is itself a star, and Aoki–Escolar–Tada Theorem 4.1 supplies monotonicity.
residual_risks: The finite verifier through r=6 is only supporting evidence; the general proof is combinatorial.

evidence: Aoki gives the general saturated-pair formula and a grid application; Aoki–Escolar–Tada gives monotonicity and zero-dimensional cases, not the arbitrary-star evaluation.

originality.rationale: Aoki's theorem is a general formula, but it does not state or tabulate the star value or the maximum-Hasse-degree lower bound. The star computation requires identifying all intervals, proving the uniform upper bound and exhibiting a saturated extremizer; the degree corollary then combines that exact computation with a separate monotonicity theorem. Exact/synonymous searches and Resultary returned the assigned star record and related extremal/weak-order records, not an earlier star formula. Under the requested implication test, the general formula is the tool rather than a statement that already contains the evaluated invariant.
residual_risks: Because Aoki's general formula is extremely recent, parallel unpublished evaluations of stars remain possible.

value.rationale: The exact orientation-independent star family is a natural branching test case, and the derived maximum-Hasse-degree lower bound is a reusable structural consequence that is sharp on stars. It also exhibits unbounded interval-relative complexity inside a hereditary-incidence-algebra family. This is a motivated exact invariant rather than an arbitrary finite slice.

final_claim: For every orientation of the star Hasse graph K_{1,r}, the interval endomorphism algebra has global dimension max(2,r), hence interval-resolution global dimension max(0,r-2); consequently every finite connected poset Q has interval-resolution global dimension at least max(0,Delta(Q)-2).
limitations: The star formula is explicitly an evaluation/application of Aoki's very recent general theorem, not a replacement for it.
